title: Is Malaysia's economy growing?
subtitle: Yes. GDP grew 5.4% in early 2026, and services now run the show.
question: Is Malaysia's economy growing, what is the GDP growth rate, and how big is the economy?
answer: Yes. Malaysia's economy grew 5.4% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026, after 5.2% growth across the whole of 2025, faster than most advanced economies. In real terms the economy is worth about RM1.74 trillion a year. Almost 60% of it is services; manufacturing adds another quarter. Agriculture, once the backbone, is now just 6%.

takeaways: **The economy is still growing.** Real GDP rose 5.4% year-on-year in Q1 2026, extending a solid run of 5.2% in 2025 and 5.2% in 2024, quicker than most developed economies.
**Services are the engine.** At about RM1.03 trillion, services, retail, finance, tourism, transport, telecoms and government, make up nearly 60% of the economy.
**Manufacturing is the second pillar** (about RM399 billion, ~23%), the same electronics and machinery that dominate Malaysia's exports.
**The Covid scar was deep.** GDP shrank 5.5% in 2020, the worst contraction since the 1998 Asian financial crisis, then rebounded 9.0% in 2022 as the economy reopened.
**Malaysia has left the farm behind.** Agriculture is now just ~6% of GDP. The country has shifted decisively from a commodity economy to services and manufacturing.

faq.q: What is Malaysia's GDP growth rate?
faq.a: Malaysia's real GDP grew 5.4% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026, following full-year growth of 5.2% in 2025 and 5.2% in 2024, according to DOSM data on data.gov.my.
About RM1.74 trillion a year in real (inflation-adjusted) terms in 2025, per DOSM. In nominal (current-price) terms it is larger, roughly RM1.9 trillion.

faq.q: What is the biggest sector of Malaysia's economy?
faq.a: Services, at about RM1.03 trillion, nearly 60% of GDP. Manufacturing is second at around RM399 billion (about 23%), followed by agriculture, mining and construction.
By most measures yes: growth of 5.4% in early 2026 is above the global average and faster than most advanced economies, driven by services and a strong manufacturing and export base.

faq.q: How much did Malaysia's economy shrink during Covid?
faq.a: Real GDP contracted 5.5% in 2020, its worst year since the 1998 Asian financial crisis, before recovering and growing 9.0% in 2022.

faq.q: Where does this GDP data come from?
faq.a: From the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), published as official open data on data.gov.my. Quarterly figures run to Q1 2026 and annual sector figures to 2025.
